title: The Jackett Ranch
indexLine: My dad bought a block of land in Colorado in the '70s and has never seen it. I went to look.
homeLine: My dad bought a block of land in Colorado in the '70s and has never seen it. I went to look, then told the internet he's giving it away.
metaTitle: The Jackett Ranch, Colorado | Tommy Jackett
metaDescription: How my dad bought a block of land in Colorado for $5,000, never saw it, and why I told the internet he's giving it away.
body: Imagine if you could buy a block of land. 8.5 acres, $5,000, no deposit, $50 a week.
That's exactly what my dad did in the '70s. A block in Colorado, paid off over 10 years, and the deed turned up in 1985. He has never seen it.

So I found a mate who was down for a road trip. A 15-hour flight from Melbourne to San Francisco, 2,500 kilometres of driving, all to see if my family was sitting on a gold mine. The local real estate agent took us out in his Jeep, because our hire car wouldn't have made it.
It was a steep hill. No water, no electricity, and it snows about half the year.

The block was one of nearly 8,000 cut from a huge ranch. Thousands of people bought them, and most are still empty. As I say in the film, the Forbes family are up $175 million and the Jacketts are down $5K, plus the taxes each year.
Dad's cutting his losses. He didn't think anyone would want it, so I put it on the internet and let the internet do what it does best. At the end of Part 1 I offered it up for free.
More soon.

title: Have A Crack
indexLine: Why I think giving things a go beats waiting until you're ready.
homeLine: The video where I say what I actually believe about giving things a go.
metaTitle: Have A Crack: why giving it a go matters | Tommy Jackett
metaDescription: Why having a crack is the best decision you'll ever make. The 2023 video where I say what I believe about giving things a go.
body: I've been having a crack for years.
In 2023 I made a video about it. The idea is simple. "It doesn't always unfold as you may have hoped, but the success is found in the action of giving it a crack."

Here's my proof. If I'd never had a crack at making a web series in America, I don't think I ever would have found my love for filmmaking. I've hosted breakfast radio in Shepparton. I've fished bikes out of the Yarra. Some of it worked, plenty of it didn't, and every bit of it led to the next thing.
It's all about finding success one crack at a time, and it really sums up my approach. If you're feeling unsure or stuck or don't know where to start, just get out there and have a crack.

title: Domino's promised 100 slices of pepperoni
metaTitle: Domino's pepperoni count, 53 slices | Tommy Jackett
metaDescription: Domino's promised 100 slices of pepperoni on its Pepperoni Deluxe. I counted them on camera and got 53. Here's the video.
body: Domino's said its Pepperoni Deluxe was topped right to the edge with 100 slices of pepperoni. So I counted them.
I counted them on camera. The total was 53. "That's all 53 slices of pepperoni on the pepperoni Deluxe at Domino's where they promise 100 slices of pepperoni. Case closed."
It's not the first time I've counted something to check a claim. In 2016 I counted the steps at the 1000 Steps in Victoria. My count was 776, and Pedestrian TV ran the story.
I posted the pepperoni video in March 2023. It's a minute and a half.

title: The 7-Eleven coffee cup
indexLine: A $3 coffee, a $2 cup, and one question.
homeLine: I tipped a $3 coffee into a $2 cup to see if it would fit.
metaTitle: The 7-Eleven coffee cup test | Tommy Jackett
metaDescription: I tipped a $3 7-Eleven coffee into a $2 cup to see if it would fit. Here's the video, and what came next.
body: So we've got a $2 coffee cup, and we're going to tip the $3 into the two and find out once and for all.

That's how the video starts, and it's pretty much the whole idea. [[NEEDS TOMMY: the result, in one plain sentence, from the video itself]] I put it in the title as a rip-off, so you can guess which way it went.

It's old footage, so they may have fixed this problem. I posted it in September 2018, and a month later I made a longer one, The 7-Eleven Coffee Rabbit Hole, going further into how the cup sizes work. A couple of money blogs picked it up the next day.
The two videos have been watched more than 20,000 times between them.

title: Fishing for oBikes in the Yarra
indexLine: I went fishing for abandoned bikes in the Yarra and a company noticed.
homeLine: I went fishing for abandoned oBikes in the Yarra. Within days the company had contractors out on the river.
metaTitle: oBike fishing in the Yarra | Tommy Jackett
metaDescription: In September 2017 I went fishing for abandoned oBikes in the Yarra. Within days the company had contractors out on the river.
body: In September 2017 oBikes were everywhere in Melbourne, including the bottom of the Yarra.
I got a bit obsessed. Not with the bikes. With how everyone reacted to them. So I grabbed a hook and went fishing. I pulled out seven and put the video up.
Pedestrian TV ran it. ABC Radio Melbourne had me on Melbourne Mornings to talk about it. Within days oBike had contractors out on the river, and they pulled out more than 40 bikes.

Then it got a bit silly. I got some t-shirts printed and [[NEEDS TOMMY: the Sunrise detail, who got in touch and whether you wore one on air]]. The shirts made $1,520 [[NEEDS TOMMY: where the money went]].
In the last video I thank oBike for having bikes absolutely everywhere, and ask them to go clean them up.
In 2022 I did it again, with e-scooters. Five out of the Yarra in under two hours, and 3AW had me on with Neil Mitchell.
The first two videos have been watched more than 100,000 times between them.
